sql_schemas: table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, start_date, end_date, status, reason, manager_id, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of all leave requests for a given employee; status: filtering by pending/approved/rejected status for manager dashboards; leave_type: filtering and aggregation by leave type; manager_id: manager dashboard — all requests awaiting a specific manager's approval; (employee_id, status): compound lookup for 'my pending requests'; (manager_id, status): compound lookup for 'pending approvals assigned to me'

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, year, total_allocated, used_days, pending_days, carried_over, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id | indexes: (employee_id, leave_type, year): unique lookup for a specific employee's balance for a given leave type and year — the dominant access pattern for balance checks and deductions; employee_id: all-balances view for an employee

table leave_policies | fields: id, leave_type, days_per_year, allow_carry_over, max_carry_over_days, requires_approval, min_notice_hours, max_consecutive_days, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: unique lookup of policy by leave type name — the dominant access pattern when validating a leave request against policy rules; is_active: filtering active policies only

methods: findByEmployeeId(employeeId: string, opts?: { status?: LeaveStatus; limit?: number; offset?: number }): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>
findByManagerId(managerId: string, opts?: { status?: LeaveStatus; limit?: number; offset?: number }): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>
updateStatus(id: string, status: LeaveStatus, updatedBy: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest>
countOverlapping(employeeId: string, startDate: Date, endDate: Date, excludeId?: string): Promise<number>
findByEmployeeAndType(employeeId: string, leaveType: string, year: number): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>
deductPendingDays(employeeId: string, leaveType: string, year: number, days: number, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveBalance>
releasePendingDays(employeeId: string, leaveType: string, year: number, days: number, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveBalance>
commitUsedDays(employeeId: string, leaveType: string, year: number, days: number, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveBalance>

data_notes: All tables assume an existing `employees` table (from the employee module) with primary key `id`. The `leave_requests.manager_id` FK references the same `employees.id`. Audit records (GP-002) are handled by the existing AuditLog module — state-changing repository methods are expected to be wrapped by the service layer, which writes audit records via IAuditService. The `leave_balances` table uses a conceptual unique constraint on `(employee_id, leave_type, year)` — the `upsertBalance` method relies on this. `pending_days` tracks days requested but not yet approved/rejected; `used_days` tracks approved consumed days. `total_allocated` is the annual entitlement; `carried_over` is days brought forward from the prior year.

open_questions.question: How is the "year" boundary for leave_balances defined — calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31), fiscal year, or employee-specific anniversary year?
open_questions.impact: Determines how balances are initialized, reset, and how carry-over is applied. Affects the upsertBalance logic and any year-rollover batch process.

transaction_contract: Repository methods that participate in multi-step writes (create, updateStatus, upsertBalance, deductPendingDays, releasePendingDays, commitUsedDays) accept an optional `client: PoolClient` parameter. When omitted, the method acquires its own connection from the shared pool for single-step operations. The calling service owns the unit of work: it acquires a client from the pool, executes `BEGIN`, passes the client to every repository call in the unit, then `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK`. Specifically: (1) leave application = create leave_request + deductPendingDays on leave_balances in one transaction; (2) approval = updateStatus + releasePendingDays + commitUsedDays in one transaction; (3) rejection = updateStatus + releasePendingDays in one transaction.
